subject: Dedicated elasticity playbook and SLA alignment - Orion Health launch
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@orionhealth.com>
To: vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com
Cc: nora.yang@orionhealth.com
Date: Tue, 28 Nov 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Capacity needs for Dec launch - initial ask

Vanessa,

Thanks again for the run earlier this week. Quick summary from our side as we prep for a public beta on Dec 21: we expect a steady-state inference load of ~150 qps (avg request size ~450 tokens) with short peaks up to ~650 qps during release-day spikes (~6 hours total distributed across the day). Latency targets for user-facing features are p95 < 350ms and p99 < 800ms.

We"d prefer a Dedicated deployment for data isolation and consistent latency. Can Redwood support a baseline reserved pool plus temporary burst capacity for launch spikes? If possible we"d like guidance on:
- baseline sizing (GPU counts / preferred instance families)
- burst runway (how much extra capacity, how long, and any throttling behavior)
- any recommended prewarm / canary steps to avoid cold starts at scale

I can share our traffic curves and token distribution if helpful. Procurement (procurement@orionhealth.com) is looped for contract/commitment questions.

Samir
Head of Product, Orion Health
---
Orion Health | samir.patel@orionhealth.com

From: vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@orionhealth.com>
Cc: nora.yang@orionhealth.com, ben.carter@redwoodinference.com, karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 28 Nov 2028 11:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Capacity needs for Dec launch - initial ask

Samir — thanks for the clear numbers. High level: yes, Dedicated + burst runway is exactly how we handle release spikes. Below is a pragmatic proposal to start the conversation; I"ll loop in ops details and a commitment matrix attachment.

Proposal (rough):
- Baseline reserved: 24x A100-equivalent GPUs (predictable throughput for steady-state 150 qps).
- Burst runway: up to +60 GPUs (total up to 84) for short-term spikes; burst is enforced via a burst credit pool with a monthly cap.
- Burst window policy: automatic autoscale to burst capacity when queue latency > threshold; 72 hours of aggregate burst allowance per month with hourly granularity.
- Prewarm / canary: 48-hour staged ramp with a 10% traffic canary then 50% then full switch; we"ll provide a prewarm API to prime KV caches and warm attention kernels.

Tradeoffs and notes:
- H100 gives better per-GPU throughput for large-context models; if you"re using model variants, we can recommend the best mapping.
- Eviction priority: ephemeral burst instances are preemptible and we throttle non-prod and lower-tier routes first.

I"m attaching a commitment matrix and a high-level capacity diagram. Ben and Karthik — can you add the ops/runbook bullets and an SLA addendum we can share with procurement?

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com

From: karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com, ben.carter@redwoodinference.com
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@orionhealth.com>, nora.yang@orionhealth.com
Date: Wed, 29 Nov 2028 08:24:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Capacity needs for Dec launch - initial ask

Adding ops detail and a compact runbook draft. Key assumptions: model = LLM-v2-32k, typical prompt 450 tokens, responses ~200 tokens, steady-state tail behavior as Samir described.

Autoscale / burst governance (draft):
- Scaling units: 1 unit = 1 GPU (A100 equivalent baseline). We"ll publish per-request token cost estimates and effective RPS per GPU for your model.
- Triggering signals: sustained queue depth > 20 requests for 60s OR p95 latency > 300ms for 2 consecutive minutes -> scale +10 GPU units (bounded by available burst credits).
- Backoff: p95 < 250ms for 3 minutes -> remove 10 GPU units. Minimum cooldown 3 minutes between scale actions to avoid oscillation.
- Prewarming: warm KV cache + allocate empty model KV for each new instance; prewarm API call will accept a traffic replay payload (we recommend 1 hour of sampled traffic during the 48h prewarm).
- Burst credit accounting: credits consumed per GPU-hour at time-of-burst; 72 credited hours/month are included in the proposed tier. Excess billed at on-demand rate or capped and throttled per agreement.
- Eviction & graceful degradation: we will define route priority labels. During eviction we will: 1) stop lower-priority background inference; 2) shed long-running batch jobs; 3) throttle non-essential routes before user-facing routes.

Operational hooks we recommend Orion provide:
- In-product feature flag to shift a percentage of traffic to the dedicated endpoint (for canary phases).
- Shared telemetry: token-level logs for the canary window and a short sampling config for production (privacy-preserving).

I"ve attached a one-page ops diagram and a proposed SLA addendum (v2) with the burst credit table. Ben, please add any SRE on-call expectations and runbook links.

—Karthik
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com

From: ben.carter@redwoodinference.com <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com, karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@orionhealth.com>, procurement@orionhealth.com
Date: Thu, 30 Nov 2028 10:10:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Capacity needs for Dec launch - initial ask

Quick operational additions:
- On-call and escalation: for the launch day we recommend a 24-hour on-call window that includes one Redwood duty SRE and one SE from your side. We"ll provide a runbook Slack channel, and a short paging policy.
- Canary checklist (examples): smoke generate, token-stability check, p95/p99 snapshot comparisons, KV cache hit-rate target (>85%).
- Cost smoothing: if Orion wants a firm monthly cap, we can move burst hours into a refundable credit ledger to avoid unexpected bills; otherwise excess is billed at our on-demand rate.

Procurement: I"ll attach the SLA addendum and the commitment matrix for signatures. If procurement needs language changes for burst credit refunds (example: convert unused credits to bill credits), flag them and we"ll route to legal.

Ben Carter
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com

From: procurement@orionhealth.com <procurement@orionhealth.com>
To: vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com, ben.carter@redwoodinference.com
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@orionhealth.com>, lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 03 Dec 2028 13:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated elasticity playbook and SLA alignment - Orion Health launch

Vanessa / Ben,

Procurement here. We reviewed the SLA addendum and commitment matrix. A few points before we kick the DocuSign:
1) We need a firm monthly burst-credit visibility report (CSV) delivered within 72 hours after month-end.
2) Requesting a 30% cap on peak auto-bursting per hour to limit cost runaway — i.e., at most 30% of baseline reserved GPUs may be added automatically without manual approval; the remainder requires a one-click approval from our billing admin.
3) Please confirm the refund policy for unused burst credits (we propose unused credits rollover for three months or converted to bill credits).

If those are acceptable we"ll sign and send our PO.

Thanks,
Procurement Team
Orion Health (procurement@orionhealth.com)

From: vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: procurement@orionhealth.com, Samir Patel <samir.patel@orionhealth.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwoodinference.com, karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com, lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 03 Dec 2028 15:08:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated elasticity playbook and SLA alignment - Orion Health launch

Procurement — appreciate the clear asks, all reasonable. Confirmations:
- We will provide a monthly burst-credit CSV report within 48 hours of month-end (we can shorten to 24h for an expanded enterprise package).
- Hourly automatic burst cap: we can set the default automatic cap at 30% of baseline (per your request). We"ll expose a single-click approval flow in the Redwood Console for the remainder of the burst window that maps to your billing admin identity.
- Unused credits: we will roll over unused burst credits for up to 3 months; alternatively you can elect to convert them to bill credits at the end of each month — we"ll include both options in the DocuSign.

Next step: I"m attaching the SLA addendum v2 with the updated tables and the commitment matrix. If everything looks good Samir / procurement, please sign via the DocuSign link and share the PO; we"ll schedule the 48-hour prewarm window and practice canary the week of Dec 11.

Thanks — excited to get Orion launched.

Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com
